# ppt-remote

> Free presentation remote that runs in the browser. Open a PDF or PowerPoint deck, then change slides, point and draw with hand gestures in front of your webcam, or scan a QR code to turn your phone into a clicker and gyroscope laser pointer. No app, no clicker, no install. Live at https://ppt-remote.onrender.com/ (formerly Signify 2.0).

Key facts:

- Use it: open https://ppt-remote.onrender.com/ on the laptop, drop in a deck, scan the QR code with a phone, press Present. Press `F` for fullscreen.
- Phone remote: Next, Prev, Pointer (hold and aim the phone; drag down to draw), Undo, Clear, Blank, plus settings for sensitivity, acceleration, smoothing, drift correction and axis inversion.
- Laser pointer: driven by the phone's gyroscope; visible in the room and on screen-shared video calls. Needs HTTPS.
- Hand gestures (defaults, customisable): pinky up = next slide, thumb up = previous, index = point, thumb + index = draw, index + middle + ring = undo, index + middle + pinky = show text. Tracked with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker in a Web Worker.
- Files: PDFs render in the browser with pdf.js and are never uploaded. PPT, PPTX and ODP are converted to PDF on the server with headless LibreOffice; animations are flattened.
- Latency: after QR pairing the phone talks to the laptop directly over Wi-Fi with WebRTC DataChannels (8-byte pointer frames, ~2–10 ms); falls back to a server relay on isolated networks.
- Privacy: webcam video never leaves the laptop.
- Keyboard: → / Space / PgDn next, ← / PgUp previous, B blank, T text, Z undo, C clear, F fullscreen, P pairing QR.
- Stack: Go server (pairing, WebRTC signaling, relay, PPTX conversion) and React + TypeScript frontend (Vite). Self-host with Docker or the included Render Blueprint.
- Free tier note: the hosted site can take 30–50 s to wake up after being idle.
